neurosem_findings.where: Acronym ambiguity of 'SEM' in neuroscience literature (OpenAlex counts)
neurosem_findings.finding: OpenAlex title/abstract counts on 2026-09-13: 'scanning electron microscopy' AND neuron = 1232; 'structural equation model' AND neuron = 78 (AND neuroscience = 173); 'standard error of the mean' AND neuron = 167. Overall 'scanning electron microscopy (SEM)' = 264718; 'structural equation modeling (SEM)' = 94565; 'standard error of the mean (SEM)' = 1505 (abstract mentions only; figure legends are not indexed, where SEM-as-standard-error is ubiquitous). Existing uses add spectral element method (NeuroSEM, CMAME) and search engine marketing (neurosem.com). A neuroscience reader seeing 'NeuroSEM' is more likely to parse SEM as microscopy, statistics or structural equation modelling than as 'semantic'; the intended 'semantic drift' meaning is not recoverable from the name.

neurosem_verdict: Not recommended to keep. No package, docs project, GitHub account or US federal wordmark named NeuroSem was found, so the registry namespace itself was open on 2026-09-13. The problem is scholarly and search confusion: (1) a 2025 CMAME journal article plus arXiv preprint and code repository already name a computational simulation framework 'NeuroSEM'; (2) an active GPL-3.0 GitHub project with the identical spelling 'NeuroSem' in neuroscience-plus-language-models was pushed today and reports a manuscript in submission freeze; (3) a neuromarketing company trades as NeuroSEM and has held neurosem.com since 2013; (4) 'Neuro-SEM' is already used for structural-equation-modelling neuroscience, and 'neuro-semantic(s)' already means word-meaning decoding in neuroscience and a coaching movement derived from neuro-linguistic programming; (5) 'SEM' is heavily overloaded in neuroscience. Together these make a TCBB-style paper and software citation hard to find and easy to mis-attribute, and the name does not signal the method (behavioural regression testing of neuron models).

recommendation: Change the name before Milestone 1 creates the package (src/neurosem/, CLI 'neurosem', CITATION.cff). Primary suggestion: PerturbPrint (package/CLI 'perturbprint'). It maps one-to-one onto the handoff's defined term 'perturbation fingerprint', and no package, repository, account, paper, arXiv record, DataCite DOI or US federal wordmark with that name was found in the sources checked. A descriptive subtitle can carry the rest of the method (for example, mutation-calibrated stimulation batteries for detecting behavioural regressions in neuron models). Runner-up: DriftClamp, which is equally clean in the sources checked but risks confusion with recording drift and physical clamp setups. Neither name has been checked against EUIPO, Semantic Scholar, Zenodo's own API, DBLP, Google Scholar, IEEE Xplore, ACM DL, non-US trademark offices or common-law use, and none of the checks establish legal availability. The final choice is Neel's decision. Registries can change, so re-run the PyPI, conda-forge, GitHub and USPTO checks on the chosen name immediately before M1. No name has been registered or reserved.

unverifiable: Semantic Scholar: HTTP 429 on every attempt for NeuroSem and all six alternatives (no API key).
Zenodo API: HTTP 504 on every attempt; DataCite was used as a partial substitute, but Zenodo records without DataCite-visible metadata may be missed.
arXiv API: HTTP 429; the arXiv web search page was used instead (all-fields search only).
DBLP: anti-bot interstitial returned; not searched.
Google Scholar, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library: not queried directly in this task (expected automated-access blocks); covered only indirectly via WebSearch, Crossref and OpenAlex.
EUIPO trademarks: eSearch is a JavaScript app; no results retrieved. WIPO Global Brand Database and national offices other than USPTO not checked.
USPTO: queried through the backend endpoint used by the tmsearch web app (undocumented); results cover US federal applications/registrations only, not state or common-law marks.

Domain availability: rdap.org does not resolve .io (validated with github.io returning 404), so .io results are uninformative; .org/.com RDAP 404s were not confirmed with a registrar; .ai and .net were only HTTP-probed.
GitHub search covers public repositories only; private repositories, GitLab, Bitbucket, Codeberg and SourceForge were not searched.
Company registries (e.g. Companies House, US state registries) were not searched for NeuroSEM or alternatives.
Descriptions of neurosem.com, Neuro-Semantics (L. Michael Hall / ISNS) and the OSTI/ScienceDirect pages come from WebFetch/WebSearch summaries rather than full-page reads.
Whether the vafaei-ar/NeuroSem manuscript will be published under that name, and its venue, is unknown.
